results.content:
It was extremely difficult just to create a decent 2–3 second cinematic opening hook. The platform constantly fights against the workflow instead of supporting it. Scene durations are also ignored regularly. Even when I specify exact timing for scenes, Revid changes the pacing anyway, forcing additional editing afterward.  
  
Another extremely frustrating issue is that upgrading from the Basic generation options to the more expensive Pro generation mode did not improve the quality at all. In fact, this is where I lost the most credits. Large generations costing 1200+ credits frequently produced completely unusable videos. That meant I had to regenerate entire videos again and again or manually replace scene after scene trying to fix broken outputs. [...] What makes this more frustrating is that Revid sometimes clearly understands the topic because it generated a thumbnail for the snake video that actually matched the idea perfectly. The title and thumbnail recognized the concept correctly, yet the actual generated video completely changed the subject into random unrelated content. It honestly feels like the AI decides on its own what kind of video it wants to make instead of following the user’s instructions.  
  
Another major problem is editing. Revid generates what feels like a rough RAW version of a video, but most of it is unusable and requires constant corrections outside the platform. Thumbnails also need to be remade repeatedly because they often do not properly match the final topic or quality expected. [...] ## I subscribed to the Elite plan… it wasn't worth it.
I subscribed to the Elite plan expecting a professional AI video generation tool, but honestly Revid AI has been one of the most frustrating platforms I’ve used, especially considering the $89/month price tag.  
  
The biggest issue is that the AI simply does not follow prompts or scripts correctly. I created a detailed video about giant snakes and prehistoric serpents, and the generated scenes were completely unrelated to what I described.

Users discussing Revid AI on Reddit-style forums and public review platforms often bring up credits, pricing, inconsistent AI output, reliability, customer support, or the fact that AI videos still need manual strategy. In other words, Revid can speed up production, but it does not automatically create a strong channel or make every video stand out.

That is the main takeaway: Revid AI is good for drafts and volume, but human direction still matters.
